_comment: Honest readings. A percentage is only worth printing while it still describes the window it is drawn under, so every port agrees on when it may NOT be printed. Two things end a reading: the payload carried no number for that limit (percentKnown false - the endpoint ships kinds nobody has enabled as null placeholders, and drawing them as 0 % reads as a full tank), and the window's reset instant has passed (the endpoint keeps the old figure until the next window opens). Both give `–` and an EMPTY bar - never a stale percentage that looks exactly like a fresh one. Pinned across lib/pure/usage.js (GNOME), claude-code/normalize.js (CLI + MCP + status line) and ClaudeUsageCore/Model.swift (macOS).

normalize.name: a null placeholder is no reading, not 0 %
a percent of the wrong JSON type is no reading either
a missing percent key is no reading
the legacy fields only produce a card when they carry a number, so it is always a reading

cases.name: a live window reads its percentage
no reset at all is still a reading - nothing says the window is gone
an unparseable reset is not a rolled-over window
percent is clamped, like everywhere else
no number in the payload: en dash and an empty bar, never 0 %
the window has reset: the stored percentage belongs to a window that is gone
exactly at the reset instant the window is already gone
sub-second before the reset the countdown already reads 0, so the reading is gone too
a full second before the reset it is still a reading
both at once: the rolled-over window is the reason reported
